level: stop-fence design slice 2: single-machine shared-admission and migration exclusive-fence prototype on synthetic homes
componentAcceptance: verified with real child-process holders on Windows and Linux machines: drain, gate race, concurrent coordinators and crash takeover
productAcceptance: prototype for protocol-participating processes only; it is not a stop-write proof for old programs or third parties and does not advance activationSupported
implementation: Shared admission (a protocol host before creating any writer): under a claimed-directory guard mutex, refuse when a durable intent or exclusive claim exists, otherwise create the shared claim — the check-and-create pair is atomic under the guard, closing the read-gate → create-writer gap.

Coordinator exclusive: persist the durable intent under the guard (this alone blocks every new shared admission and outlives coordinator death), drain live shared holders with per-holder observation, then re-take the guard, re-verify no new shared claim appeared and the intent is ours, and create the exclusive claim. Release is owner-checked and removes intent plus claim.

Crash takeover: a live foreign coordinator (with or without its exclusive claim) answers MIGRATION_FENCE_BUSY; a verifiably dead coordinator's intent keeps blocking writers until a takeover coordinator reclaims its stale exclusive claim after death verification and re-runs the drain.

Guard discipline: dead-owner guards are reclaimed after identity verification; a guard owned by the current process is treated as stale cleanup residue (withGuard is never re-entered recursively) and reclaimed too — this closed a real Windows self-deadlock found during development. Guard removal retries against transient directory locks. Linux claims carry /proc start-tick identity (PID-reuse safe); Windows keeps pid-only identity as a documented prototype limitation.

platforms.rootRegression: 1844 tests, 1776 pass, 0 fail, 68 skipped, exit 0 (log: tmp/integration/migration-fence-root-regression.log); the suite is registered in npm test and Windows/Ubuntu CI

preservedFailures: Development found four real defects, each reproduced then fixed: (1) a protocol-deadlock by test design — the drain waits for holders while the test awaited the drain before releasing them (fixed to the real timing: coordinator requests stop, holders exit, then the fence resolves); (2) a Windows guard self-deadlock — a transient directory-lock failure left the guard behind and a later withGuard in the same process respected its own residue forever (fixed with self-residue reclaim plus removal retries); (3) an assertion race against the asynchronous intent write (fixed with a bounded poll); (4) an exited() helper that attached exit listeners after the event had fired and never resolved (fixed with an already-exited check). None were silenced.
limitations: Participation is voluntary and same-machine: old programs, third parties and other machines are outside this fence (slices 4 and 5); pid liveness is not a kernel write barrier.
Windows claims carry no start-tick identity, so PID reuse inside a claim's lifetime is a documented prototype limitation there.

This prototype does not wire the product startup gate, does not perform capture/commit, and stopWriteProvable-style honesty is kept: the fence never claims a stop-write proof. activationSupported stays false.
